answers.answer: For four players select 3 Pods randomly. Place the lowest-numbered in Section A, next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked. The bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (so 7 Adults).

Remove Corporate and Personal Objectives showing a player count above the actual count, shuffle each deck separately and deal each player one of each face down. At the First Encounter, each player chooses one of the two and removes the other face down unseen. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this choice.

Discard the played Action card plus exactly two additional Action cards for its printed cost 2. The two Contamination cards cannot pay costs. If the Action card offers sections separated by OR, choose one section.
answers.evidence: Action Cost; Actions from Action cards

answers.answer: Fire damage to a Character is taken at the end of their own round: one Light Wound. Having taken one Action and then passing ends that round, so they take it then. After passing they cannot take normal Actions for the rest of the Player Phase, and later players' rounds do not burn them again that turn. On passing they may discard any number of hand cards.

On entry, flip an unexplored tile face up and resolve its Exploration token, then remove the token to the box. Set the Item count by rotating the tile to align the token's number with the board counter, except Nest and Slime Room. Apply the symbol: Silence cancels the Noise roll; Danger resolves its movement/noise effect instead; Slime adds a marker; Fire or Malfunction is placed in that Room; Door goes in the Corridor used to enter. After exploration, roll Noise only if the entered Room is empty; if anyone is already there, no roll. A Noise result 1–4 marks that numbered connected Corridor (including Technical if Entrance); if already marked, resolve Encounter. Silence means nothing, unless your Slime converts it to Danger. Danger moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room; if none eligible, mark every unmarked connected Corridor.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the normal post-move Noise roll with placing one Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination. It is forbidden in Combat and if all destination-connected Corridors already have Noise. Normal movement restrictions apply: Closed Doors block crossing, and miniatures cannot stop in Corridors.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors

answers.answer: A number rolled for a Corridor already containing Noise causes an Encounter. First discard all Noise in Corridors connected to the Room, including Technical Corridors if connected. Draw one bag token and place its matching Intruder in the Room; set a drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag. Compare its number with the triggering player's hand size counting Action and Contamination cards: fewer cards than the token number causes a Surprise Attack against the triggering Character. Contamination cards count toward this comparison, though they cannot pay costs. A Noise marker in Technical Corridors is shared across all its entrances.

Danger moves ALL neighboring Intruders that are not in Combat with a Character into the destination. If there are none eligible, place Noise in every connected Corridor lacking a marker (including Technical Corridors with an Entrance). An Intruder moving into a Character's Room is not an Encounter. A Character with Slime resolves Silence as Danger.

If an Encounter draws Blank, no miniature appears: put Noise in every Corridor connected to the Room, add an Adult to the bag only if Blank was the last token and an Adult is available, then return Blank to the bag. In bag development, Blank adds an available Adult token (or does nothing if none are available) and returns to the bag; it does not create an Encounter.
answers.evidence: Blank token in an Encounter; bag development

answers.answer: Intruders cannot pass a Closed Door: the two moving from the same Room destroy the Door simultaneously and both stay where they were. Destroyed Doors lie flat and cannot be closed again (except Plasma Torch). A Noise-triggered Intruder appearance comes through regardless of a Closed Door.

When an Intruder enters a Technical Corridors Entrance, remove its miniature, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the bag. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors (exceptions are Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action and Technical Corridor Plans); Doors can never be placed there.

Shoot costs 1 Action card and 1 Ammo, requires a Weapon in hand and an Intruder in your Room; choose target, discard Ammo, roll. Melee costs 1 Action card, draws a Contamination card onto your Action discard pile, and targets an Intruder in your Room. A missed Melee inflicts a Serious Wound; double-hit is only 1 Injury in Melee. A Shoot miss has no Wound penalty. The summary does not separately specify a Melee miss's Contamination handling beyond the card draw cost.

Larva and Egg die at 1 Injury. Creeper or Adult: draw one Intruder Attack card and compare blood value to total Injuries; blood less than or equal to Injuries means death. Queen: draw two cards and sum blood; sum less than or equal to total Injuries means death. A dead Creeper, Adult, Breeder or Queen leaves a Carcass in the Room; Larva does not. If any relevant injury-check card has a Retreat arrow, retreat replaces numerical death/endurance; for Queen, either of its two cards with arrow triggers retreat.
answers.evidence: Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat

answers.answer: Escape is a Movement Action costing 1. Before moving, take one Intruder Attack per Intruder in the starting Room, in size order largest first: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva. Escape attacks target the escaper. If they die, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, complete movement to the neighboring unexplored Room, reveal/resolve its Exploration token, and make Noise if it is empty (unless exploration suppresses or replaces the roll).

With several Characters present, target the one whose player has fewest Action cards; ties go to the First Player token or next in turn order. A Surprise Attack instead targets the Character who triggered the Encounter; an Escape attack targets the escaper. For non-Larva, draw an Attack card: matching Intruder symbol is a hit and resolves its effect, otherwise miss; ignore blood. Larva draws no Attack card: remove its miniature from the board, put it on the target's board, and give the target a Contamination card. If target already has a Larva, the attacker disappears, existing Larva stays, and target only gains Contamination (no automatic death). Contamination goes on top of their Action discard pile.

Dressing a Serious Wound turns off its effect but it still counts toward the three-wound limit; at three Serious Wounds any additional Wound kills, even if one is dressed. Three Light Wounds convert to a Serious Wound (clear Light track). Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound, as specified. On death, place a Character Corpse Object in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.

Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in hand; remove non-Infected scanned cards. An Infected result leaves that card and places a Larva, or kills the Character and places a Creeper in the Room if a Larva was already on their board. Surgery scans every Contamination card in deck, hand and discard, removes all Infected cards, removes a Larva if present, then inflicts one Light Wound and forces a pass; shuffle all cards including the whole hand and remaining Contamination into the Action deck, leaving the hand empty until next turn.

In a Room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee at the Eggs; each Injury destroys one Egg. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor Wound. Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and Molotov 1, thrown as if an Intruder were in the Room. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg each Fire Damage step (2 if Vulnerability to Fire is discovered). After every attempt to destroy an Egg, roll Noise. When no Eggs remain on the Intruder board, the Nest is destroyed and marked with one Injury. Contamination on a successful Egg Melee is unresolved in this summary.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest; Vulnerability to Fire

answers.answer: All Pods begin Locked; they must be unlocked and have a free space. Pay 2 Action cards for the Evacuation Section Room Action. You cannot enter if an Intruder or Malfunction is in that Section. Roll Noise first; an Intruder appearing or present makes entry fail. Each Pod fits two Characters; Heavy Objects do not use Character spaces. After boarding, you may launch immediately (Pod and occupants leave play, count as arriving on Earth, but still face Contamination and Objective checks), or wait and pass. At the start of your first round each later Player Phase, choose to wait/pass, launch, or exit free to the Section Room and take a full two-Action round. You remain present for bag-development Noise rolls while waiting; a second boarder may launch immediately with both; an Intruder appearing in the Section returns waiting Pod occupants to the Room. A Malfunction while waiting still allows waiting, launch, or exit but prevents new entry.

Victory checks are Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. Two or three Damaged Engines make the ship explode and kill everything aboard, including sleepers and Intruders; launched Pod passengers are away. A non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters, but does not destroy the ship or kill Intruders; Quarantine survives if destination is Mars. For each survivor, including Pod passengers: if no Larva, scan all Contamination in deck, hand and discard; if none are Infected, no four-card draw. If any is Infected or a Larva is present, shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from those zones together and draw four; any Contamination among four kills, none means survival. Then check Objectives. Pod passengers must do this check.

Shuffle Room 2 tiles face down and randomly place one at each 2 slot, return extras unseen; do the same with all Room 1 tiles at 1 slots. Shuffle Exploration tokens unseen, place one face down on each Room tile and return extras. Place one random Coordinates card face down by Cockpit; Destination marker begins on B. For each Engine, shuffle its Working and Damaged tokens face down and stack on matching space; top is true status. Intruder board begins with 5 Eggs and 3 random Weakness cards face down. Time begins on green space. Setup also specifies Escape Pods and bag as separately described.

Deal Help cards numbered 1 through player count randomly; that number assigns Player Number, choice order and matching Inventory. Deal one Corporate and one Personal Objective before character draft. Shuffle draft cards; Player 1 draws two and reveals both, keeps one, shuffles other back; proceed in Player Number order. Each gets Character board, miniature in Hibernatorium, shuffled 10-card Action deck, Starting Weapon in a Hand slot loaded to capacity, and two inactive Quest Items horizontal beside board. Place blue Character Corpse in Hibernatorium; first dead body found uses that blue token. Quest Items are not active initially; unlock by their mini-quests.

At the start of each Player Phase, every player draws to 5 (or 6 with Cabins); pass First Player token left after drawing except first game turn. If drawing with an empty Action deck, shuffle discard into a new deck and draw. Used/discarded Actions go face up to that Character's discard; gained Contamination goes atop it. Item/Event/Attack/Wound discards go to their matching discard spaces; ordinary discards are face up. Search/Storage rejected Item returns face down to bottom of that deck.

Event Phase: advance Time and active Self-Destruct; Intruders in Combat attack; Intruders in Fire take one Injury and resolve Injury Effect; draw and resolve Event movement, then its effect; then bag development. On Event movement, every Intruder matching the card symbol and not in a Room with any Character moves through the numbered Corridor; if it indicates Technical Corridors, remove miniature and return token to bag. Event deck runs out: shuffle Event discards into a new deck. Intruder Attack deck runs out: shuffle its discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Event Phase; Intruder Attack

answers.answer: Bag development draws one token: Larva is removed and an Adult is added; Creeper is removed and a Breeder added; Adult returns immediately to bag before all players roll Noise in order (skip Combat), and an Encounter may draw that same token; Breeder makes all eligible players roll Noise then returns; Queen: if a Character is in Nest, place Queen and resolve Encounter, otherwise add an Egg, then return Queen; Blank adds an available Adult and returns. Tokens removed for Larva/Creeper development leave the bag. Turn ends only after all development and resulting encounters resolve.

There are eight Fire and eight Malfunction markers. Trying to place a ninth of either ends game: ship explodes/loses hull integrity, everyone on board dies. Only one marker of a kind per Room; extra placements do nothing; discarded markers return to pool. At hull loss all aboard, awake or hibernating, die, and everything else aboard including Intruders dies. Already-hibernating sleepers are unaffected by later Hibernatorium Malfunction, but ship destruction kills them.
answers.evidence: Fire markers; Malfunction markers; End of the game

answers.answer: Malfunction disables that Room's Action, its Computer, and Searching remains usable. It cannot be placed in Nest, Slime Room, or unexplored Rooms. It does not alter an Engine token/status; Engine status is never affected by Room Malfunction. It does not affect already-hibernating Characters in Hibernatorium.

Normal Item cards are hidden in the Inventory holder; others see backs/colors, and there is no Inventory size limit. Any Item use must be shown to all. Heavy Items and Objects are public and occupy one of two Hand slots; drop one before taking a third. Add-type Items attach to another card and act as one. Duct Tape combines two Heavy Items in one Hand slot, never Objects. The summary states these rules but does not specify every individual Item's hidden/visible category beyond that distinction.

Voluntarily dropping is free at any time on your turn: dropped Objects remain in the Room; dropped Item cards are lost/discarded. Found Weapons from Search start with 1 Ammo; they can never exceed printed capacity. Starting Weapon begins loaded to its Ammo capacity.

Search is an Action card: choose the deck matching Room color (Red Military, Yellow Technical, Green Medical); white Room permits any of three; Blue Crafted is never searched. Draw two from one chosen deck, keep one and return the other face down to bottom. Each Search lowers Item Counter by one; zero means no more ordinary Search (Scout Scavenging exception). Special Rooms start explored and do not allow Search; Nest and Slime Room explicitly prohibit Search.

Craft Item is a Basic Action costing one Action card; discard two Item cards whose blue component icons match the Crafted card's two gray icons. Result must be available. You may inspect the Craft deck at any time. Crafted Items and components: Antidote flame + medical cross; Taser battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov flame + folded cloth/fabric.

Only the Trade initiator spends the Action; any Characters in the Room may trade with each other, including those who did not initiate. Trades require agreement, and Items/Objects may be given for nothing; empty Trade without intent to exchange is disallowed, though honest talks can end without trade. Characters cannot exchange Ammo. A Heavy Item found by Search does not require a separate Pick Up Action; Pick Up applies to Objects only.
answers.evidence: Trade; Empty Actions; Heavy Items and Objects

answers.answer: In Laboratory, Analyse one present Object: Character Corpse reveals Corpse Weakness, Intruder Carcass reveals Carcass Weakness, Egg reveals Egg Weakness. Leave Weakness face up on Intruder board; Object is not consumed and revealed rule benefits everyone. Discover Weakness Objective is satisfied if the corresponding Object was researched in Laboratory by anyone before game end; you need not personally research it.

Room Action normally costs 2 Action cards; you must be in the Room, cannot be in Combat, and cannot use a malfunctioning Room. A Malfunction also disables its Computer. The Computer icon itself has no additional effect described here. Fire does not prevent Room Actions or Searching; the character still suffers Fire wound after ending their round there.
Armory adds 2 Ammo to one of your Energy Weapons; it never reloads Classic Weapons and cannot raise Ammo above that Weapon's printed capacity.

Emergency Room lets you choose exactly one: Dress all Serious Wounds; Heal one Dressed Serious Wound; or Heal all Light Wounds. Dressing ignores a card's effect but does not remove the Wound or stop it counting toward the three Serious Wound limit. Duplicate Serious Wound effects do not stack, though multiple cards remain harder to remove.
Comms Room Send a Signal places a Status marker on your Character board's Signal space; it is used only for Objectives. Comms Room is always aboard in the standard game.

Fire Control chooses any one Room, discards its Fire marker if present, and makes all Intruders there run away in random directions (draw one Event card per Intruder). It also scatters Intruders when chosen Room has no Fire.

Generator Room Action initiates Self-Destruct by placing marker on first green track space, or stops it by removing marker; restarting begins again at green. Marker advances one space each Time advance. On first yellow, it can no longer be stopped and all Pods unlock; they may later be relocked, but later yellow spaces do not unlock again. Final skull space explodes ship. A hyperspace jump while active still counts as ship destroyed. A Character cannot start it if anyone is hibernating; Coolant Leak Event may start it despite sleepers.

Airlock Control targets any one OTHER Yellow Room whose connected Corridors have no Destroyed Doors. Immediately close every Door around it and place Procedure token. If all those Doors remain closed through end of current Player Phase (when all players passed), everything in Room dies and Fire there is removed. Opening any Door first cancels procedure.
Cabins passively gives a Character there with no Intruder present one extra card at the start of a new turn, making hand size 6 instead of 5. Malfunction disables it. It is not a paid Room Action.

Yes. Command Center can choose any one Room, including a distant one, and lets you choose which Doors in its connected Corridors to Open or Close. Destroyed Doors cannot be closed again, except by Plasma Torch; the summary does not give Command Center an exception.
answers.evidence: Room Actions, Command Center; Door tokens

answers.answer: Engine Control Room checks the status of all three Engines but cannot change status. The check still works if an Engine Room has a Malfunction marker; a Room Malfunction does not alter the Engine token/status.
answers.evidence: Room Actions, Engine Control Room; Malfunction markers

answers.answer: Hatch Control flips one Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. Monitoring Room secretly looks at any one unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replaces both; the player may lie about what was seen. It does not inspect an explored location.
answers.evidence: Room Actions, Hatch Control; Monitoring Room

answers.answer: Entering Room Covered With Slime automatically gives your Character a Slime marker; no Action required. No Item count is set there, Malfunction cannot be placed there, and Slime maxes at one (additional does nothing). Shower removes Slime but does not remove Fire; Fire can exist there normally.

Cockpit lets you Check Coordinates (secretly inspect card, may lie, replace and remember it) or Set Destination by moving the marker. Destination selects one of four entries on Coordinates card. You cannot set Destination with an Intruder in Cockpit or change it once anyone hibernates. Other players do not see the secretly inspected card unless you tell them.

Checking an Engine secretly looks at its top token and you may lie. Repair/Break via Repairs Action or Tools secretly examines both tokens and restacks them in any order; you need not say if status was repaired, but must announce if you changed token order. It works with Malfunction and without a prior check; Engine Control Room only checks and cannot change status.
answers.evidence: Special Rooms, Engines; Engine Control Room

answers.answer: You may try to hibernate only when Time is on a blue space, while in Hibernatorium with no Intruder or Malfunction. Pay 2 Action cards, roll Noise; an Intruder appearing/reaching the Room makes it fail. On success remove your miniature and stop participating until end checks. Once anyone hibernates, no Character may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct; Coolant Leak Event may initiate it. Later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake or harm sleepers.

At final Time space, ship jumps immediately: all awake Characters aboard die from g-force; Intruders are unharmed. If last alive, non-hibernating Character dies, hibernates or launches, end game: active Self-Destruct advances to final red space and resolves; otherwise Time advances to final red space and resolves. Normal jump does not kill Intruders. Endgame victory checks follow for survivors.

Characters cannot directly attack one another due to anti-aggression implants. They can harm others indirectly, for example lock them in a burning Room, activate Self-Destruct with people aboard, or throw a Grenade into a Room containing crew.

If an Adult must be placed with all eight models already on board, Adults not in Combat retreat: remove them and return their tokens to bag if possible, then place an Adult model in Encounter Room. If all eight are in Combat, the summary says the rule source does not explain the procedure; clarification is needed. An Intruder moving into an unexplored Room stays there and does not reveal the Room or token.
answers.evidence: Adult overflow; Intruders in unexplored Rooms

answers.answer: In Shoot, small curled symbol hits Larva/Creeper only (1 Injury); larger curved symbol hits Larva/Creeper/Adult only (1 Injury). Against ineligible types the result is a miss. Melee uses the same eligibility; ineligible target means miss and the Character suffers 1 Serious Wound. Eligible small/large symbols cause 1 Injury.

With no Larva, scan every Contamination card in Action deck, hand and discard. If all are non-Infected, no four-card draw is performed and cards are not removed merely for scanning non-Infected. Launched Pod passengers still undergo Contamination and Objective checks.
Antidote: flame and medical cross. Taser: battery/lightning and screwdriver/tool. Flamethrower: flame and screwdriver/tool. Molotov Cocktail: flame and folded cloth/fabric.

A Character is in Combat whenever an Intruder is in their Room; Eggs do not count. In Combat Only/Out of Combat Only markings restrict an Action or Item to the indicated state. Unmarked card and Item Actions may be used in either, subject to requirements. Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape; no Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object, Quest activation, or Room Action.
answers.evidence: In Combat / Out of Combat; Basic Actions

answers.answer: For 'Player X's Character cannot survive,' Player X must be dead at game end; you need not personally kill them. Hibernating or escaping means they survived, so does not satisfy it. 'Only survivor' means no other Character may survive. Regardless of Objective, your own Character must survive by hibernating aboard a functioning ship jumping to Earth or escaping in a Pod, and fulfill their Objective.

If Door pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on the board. Open is represented by no token; Closed by standing token; Destroyed by lying token. Maximum one token per Corridor, and Doors can never be placed in Technical Corridors.

On the first Character death, all Escape Pods automatically unlock immediately. They may be Locked again normally afterward via effects such as Hatch Control. Whether a later death re-unlocks Pods after relocking is unresolved in the source; it conflicts between 'first death' and 'any death' wording.

Storage Room Action costs 2 Action cards and lets you draw two cards from a chosen Red, Yellow or Green Item deck, keep one and put rejected card face down at the bottom of that deck. Storage Action can be repeated even when Item Counter is zero; counter only limits Search Action card. Common Room Action requirements: be in the Room, not in Combat, not in a Room with Malfunction.
answers.evidence: Room Actions; Storage FAQ ruling; Room Actions general

answers.answer: In Nest, use the Nest Room Action: pay 2 Action cards, remove one Egg token from the Intruder board into your Hand as a Heavy Object, then make a Noise roll. Picking up a previously dropped Egg token in your Room is the ordinary Pick Up Heavy Object Basic Action (cost 1 Action card); summary says this has no Noise-roll instruction. A dropped Egg does not restore the Nest's Egg total.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions; Room Actions, Nest; Eggs FAQ

answers.answer: After using a One Use Only Item Action, discard the Item card; also pay the printed Action-card cost and show the Item to all players when used.
answers.evidence: Actions from Item cards; Items and Objects

answers.answer: A Character in a launched Escape Pod counts as having arrived on Earth. This does not establish that the ship itself reached Earth: its Coordinates/Engine checks are separate, and Pod passengers are already away from ship outcomes, though still face final checks.
Yes. While waiting, you are treated as still present in the Evacuation Section for bag-development Noise rolls; skip only Characters in Combat.
Yes. A Malfunction appearing in the Section while you already wait in its Pod still permits wait, launch or exit. It prevents only new entry to Pods.
Resolve one separate Intruder Attack per Intruder in the Room before moving, in order largest first: Queen, Breeder, Adult, then Larva.
Yes. An Event that instructs removing itself is removed even if its other effect cannot be resolved.
In Adult bag development, return the drawn Adult token to the bag immediately before all eligible players roll Noise. A Noise Encounter can draw that very same Adult token.
A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door normally destroys the Door and stays. Under The Way of Moving Weakness, an affected Intruder other than Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door.
No. Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost; it affects Basic Actions generally except stated exceptions, and Basic Shoot is explicitly excluded by FAQ.
Vulnerability to Fire adds one Injury per damage instance. A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit therefore deals 3 Injuries total.
The attacking Larva disappears; the Larva already on the Character board remains. Character gains one Contamination card and is not automatically killed by this attack.

A hibernating Character does not take later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium. Ship destruction (including hull loss or two/three Damaged Engines) can still kill them, and endgame checks can kill them: a non-Earth destination kills a sleeper unless the Quarantine Objective applies to Mars, and a failed Contamination check also kills.
Yes. Coolant Leak Event may start Self-Destruct while someone hibernates. A Character starting it through Generator cannot do so while any Character is hibernating.
Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused Intruder token pool and remain reusable later; they are not removed from the game.
Fire markers may be placed in unexplored Rooms; Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms.

The first additional Light Wound converts the existing two Light Wounds into one Serious Wound (clear Light track); the second additional Light Wound then leaves one Light Wound. Final: one Serious Wound and one Light Wound.
When a Character dies, Heavy Objects drop in the Room; their Item cards disappear from the game.
No. Only the first yellow space automatically unlocks Pods. They can be relocked, and reaching subsequent yellow spaces does not unlock them again.

Destroying the ship fulfills Objectives to kill the Queen or destroy the Nest. It does not by itself make your Character a winner: your Character must survive and fulfill their Objective; ship destruction kills everyone aboard, so only eligible survivors away in Pods could remain to check their Objective.

No. Intentionally spending an empty Trade Action with no intention to exchange is an empty Action with no meaningful state change and should be disallowed. Honest negotiations may end without a trade.
Quest Item activation is a Basic Action printed on its card; it is forbidden in Combat but allowed in a Malfunctioning Room (Room Action restrictions do not apply).

In Combat, Basic Actions are limited to Shoot, Melee, and Basic Movement as Escape. You cannot Trade, Craft, or Pick Up a Heavy Object. Room Actions are forbidden. Unmarked Action-card and Item Actions may be used in or out of Combat if their requirements permit; Quest activation is a Basic Action and is forbidden in Combat.
answers.evidence: In Combat / Out of Combat; Basic Actions

answers.answer: Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone. If moving two Characters, each goes in a direction of their choice, then perform one Noise roll. If an Encounter occurs, Surprise is checked against Soldier.
Full Auto removes all Ammo, then performs one Shoot Action. Damage equals the Shoot result plus half the discarded Ammo rounded down, plus Assault Rifle's +1 bonus.

You may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing whether to use Nerves of Steel. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still suffer their effects (for example Frenzy).

Careful Movement and Reconnaissance replace/cancel automatic Silence or Danger results when those abilities reveal the token: apply the movement ability rather than the token's automatic Noise/Danger outcome. Careful Movement places its chosen Noise marker; Reconnaissance cancels the automatic result as specified by that ability.
Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat. Intercom may make another Character Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape rules and attacks.
With active Intercom, Motivation affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain's Room; those Characters can draw the Action card as its effect provides.
Entering by Technical Corridors Action or Technical Corridor Plans ignores a Door Exploration token because the entry Corridor cannot be determined; no Door is placed.

No. Interruption requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action, so a remote Order via Intercom cannot be interrupted from elsewhere. Passing does not bar Interruption; FAQ allows it after passing.

No. An empty hand after two Actions does not automatically make you pass; wait for your next round to pass. That extra round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect. Passing players still take end-of-round Fire once, but no more that turn after it.

No. Rest with no Larva before the Action cannot kill merely because several scanned cards are Infected; it places just one Larva. Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on the board before Rest, since an Infected result then kills.
Roll Noise in your own Room, not the Nest, when throwing Grenade or Molotov at Nest Eggs from another Room.
No. Intranet research still requires the Object itself to be in the Laboratory, even if Scientist is elsewhere; carrying it outside Lab cannot reveal a Weakness.

Yes. Storage Room Action may be used repeatedly at zero Item Counter, paying its usual 2 cards and normal Room restrictions. The counter limits only Search Action card; ordinary Search decreases counter by one and cannot be used at zero.
Two Eggs are destroyed per Fire Damage step when Vulnerability to Fire is discovered.
No. Once taken from Intruder board, Egg is a normal Heavy Object; dropping it in Nest does not restore the Nest's Egg total or hit points.
The affected player chooses one Action card from their own hand and discards it to their Action discard pile.
Yes. Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters.
No, Energy Charge cannot directly reload another Character's Weapon. Trade them the Charge; they use it in their own round to recharge their own Weapon.
Alcohol's Infected scan does not place a Larva; instead gain a new Contamination card.
Yes. Attaching Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to a used or empty Energy Weapon immediately grants the extra Ammo.
A newly Crafted Flamethrower starts fully loaded, not with the one Ammo that a searched Weapon starts with.
No. Hand Serious Wound does not affect Scout's Motion Scanner because it is a unique reaction, not an Item Action.

Antidote scans all your Contamination cards in hand, deck and discard, removes all Infected cards from game, gives one new Contamination card, and reshuffles that new card with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards except cards retained in hand. Then you pass; you may keep hand cards. Surgery instead scans all zones and removes Infected cards and a Larva, gives no new Contamination, inflicts one Light Wound, automatically passes and shuffles the entire hand plus remaining cards into Action deck, leaving hand empty.

On exploration: Slime marker goes on Character board; Fire and Malfunction markers go in the explored Room (Fire may also be in unexplored Rooms through effects, Malfunction may not); Door Exploration places Door in the Corridor by which you entered. Nest and Slime Room have no Item count; Slime Room cannot receive Malfunction.

During Event Phase, after Intruders in Combat attack and before Event card, each Intruder in a Room with Fire takes 1 Injury and immediately resolves normal Injury Effect, which can cause death or retreat.
No. Nest and Room Covered With Slime explicitly prohibit any Search Action.
